meta.note: Polls, markets and fundamentals (House: DDHQ) combined per race by inverse-variance weights; correlated simulation.

assumptions.name: Error no number of polls removes
assumptions.where: Uncertainty of each race's poll average, hence its weight
assumptions.how: Backtest: 213 Senate poll averages in the midterms 1998–2022 (FiveThirtyEight archive), one week before the election.

assumptions.name: Noise of a single poll
assumptions.where: Same; shrinks with the effective number of polls (√n)
assumptions.how: Same backtest, fitted together with the line above.

assumptions.name: Weighting of individual polls
assumptions.value: half-life 14 days; √sample size (cap 2,400); likely voters 1, registered 0.8, adults 0.6; partisan sponsor 0.5; older polls by the same pollster halved
assumptions.how: Common practice of poll aggregators; judgement, not calibrated.

assumptions.name: Polls from the news check
assumptions.value: added by hand where VoteHub lacks them (data/polls_manual.csv)
assumptions.where: Poll average of the contest districts; same weighting as every other poll
assumptions.how: News check of 29 Oct: NYT/Siena in PA-08 and nine partisan polls in NC-01, NY-17, PA-08 and OH-07, each checked against a second source.

assumptions.name: Exchange rate between money and polls
assumptions.where: Uncertainty of each race's market price, hence its weight
assumptions.how: Judgement, chosen so that a liquid market counts like a well-polled average (C19). Check: in the 2024 Senate races, markets one week out missed close races by 3.4 pts on average, polls in past midterms by 5.5.

assumptions.name: Penalty for a wide bid-ask spread
assumptions.how: Judgement: a wide quote says little about the price.

assumptions.name: House fundamentals
assumptions.value: Decision Desk HQ's district probabilities of 22 Oct
assumptions.where: Fundamentals input of each House race, placed on a margin scale with ±7.0 pts
assumptions.how: The course's starting point. Our own uniform-swing version missed badly in places (TX-15: 5% vs. DDHQ 45%, market 82%); see the bridge.

assumptions.name: Senate fundamentals
assumptions.value: 2024 presidential margin in the state vs. the nation + national environment + 3 pts incumbency; race error ±16 pts
assumptions.where: Fundamentals input of each Senate race
assumptions.how: Race error from the backtest (Senate midterms 1998–2022). The backtest puts incumbency near 11 pts; we keep 3 as chosen (the Senate is not scored).

assumptions.name: National environment
assumptions.where: Senate fundamentals; cross-check for the House
assumptions.how: Generic-ballot polls (D+7.4) and Kalshi's House popular-vote market (D+9.0), weighted by their uncertainty.

assumptions.name: Shared national error
assumptions.how: Backtest: the generic-ballot average missed the national House vote by 3.6 pts (RMS) in the midterms 1998–2022. Fat tails: judgement.

assumptions.name: Split of the remaining error
assumptions.where: Simulation: how strongly neighbouring races move together
assumptions.how: Judgement after Silver Bulletin's layers; the sensitivity analysis shows little effect.

assumptions.name: Least uncertainty per race
assumptions.how: Judgement: the inputs overlap (markets read polls), so their precisions cannot simply be added.

assumptions.name: Number of simulations
assumptions.how: Simulation noise ±0.4 pts or less; four re-runs with other seeds agree.

assumptions.name: Seat forecast (a)
assumptions.value: median of the simulated seat counts
assumptions.how: Teams are ranked by distance to the true count; the median minimises the expected distance.

assumptions.name: Independents
assumptions.value: Alaska's Bill Hill and Nebraska's Dan Osborn are not counted as Democrats
assumptions.how: Contest instructions (Hill); Osborn says he will not caucus with either party.
